title: IUKA BOY INJURED
full_story:
Just after 6 pm Tuesday night a four-year-old rural Iuka boy was injured when a riding lawn mower backed over him.

The Iuka Fire Department was called to the intersection of Quail Run and Kinmundy Roads.  Iuka Fire Chief Kenny Eagan says one of the boy’s legs and ankles was trapped underneath the deck and blade.  After his release from the mower the fire department and United Medical Response assisted an Air Evac helicopter to land near the home.  The boy was transported to a St. Louis Hospital for treatment.

Marion County Sheriff Kevin Cripps said the four-year-old was out in the yard and had come up behind the lawn mower unnoticed.

title: SENTENCED FOR CHILD PORN
full_story:
A district court judge sentenced an Olney man to 40 years in federal prison after he admitted to producing child pornography.

George T. Grove, 49, plead guilty to two counts of production of child pornography for creating child sexual abuse material of a 13-year-old victim.

“Sex crimes are vile offenses.  There is no amount of prison time sufficient for those who violate children,” said US Attorney Steven D. Weinhoeft.

According to court documents and information discussed at hearings, Grove admitted to creating two videos of child sexual abuse material with a cell phone of a 13-year-old victim in July 2024.  During the investigation, officers discovered the defendant was exchanging alcohol, money and drugs with minors for nude photos and sex.

The Richland County Sheriff’s Office, the Olney Police Department and Homeland Security Investigations contributed to the investigation. Assistant US Attorney David Sanders prosecuted the case.

title: WILHOUR ON DIESEL
full_story:
State Representatives and Illinois farmers Blaine Wilhour, Brad Halbrook, Brad Fritts, Charlie Meier, Chris Miller, Dan Swanson, Jason R. Bunting, and Wayne Rosenthal issued the following statement after President Donald J. Trump’s Executive Order addressing dyed diesel and Governor JB Pritzker’s corresponding action in Illinois:

“We appreciate President Trump taking the lead to provide relief to farmers facing rising diesel costs.  Farmers across Illinois are feeling the pinch from every direction.  While this is a step in the right direction, Illinois needs to take a more proactive approach to lower the cost of doing business and keep the top industry in Illinois competitive.

“Washington has made it clear that they are willing to work with states to provide relief from the diesel crisis, and Illinois should take advantage of every opportunity to lower the cost of living.  As the Illinois Farm Bureau continues to work with the Department of Revenue to fully understand any future motor fuel tax implications, we will continue to work to make life more affordable for Illinois families.  At the end of the day, a strong agricultural community means a strong Illinois.

“We are also working to address the practical challenges farmers could face when the temporary authorization expires on January 1, 2027, particularly how enforcement will be handled and what happens to residual dyed diesel that may remain in farm equipment and fuel systems after the authorization expires.”

title: TREE STAND PERMITS AVAILABLE
full_story:
Lake Shelbyville’s tree stand policy for this year will remain the same as last season’s policy.

The policy allows hunters to leave one stand up for the season, referred to as a seasonal tree stand, and/or use up to two roving stands that may be left up during archery season for no more than 72 hours without use, or the length of a three-day weekend.  Seasonal tree stands may be placed two weeks before archery season and must be removed within two weeks after archery season ends.  Archery season runs through January 17th.

Hunters wishing to purchase a seasonal tree stand permit must present a valid hunting license before a permit is issued.  Seasonal tree stand permits will be available for purchase for $30 by credit or debit card at the Lake Shelbyville Project Office, 1989 State Hwy. 16, Shelbyville, Illinois, from 8 am to 4:30 pm Monday through Friday.

Roving tree stand permits are free and may be obtained in Sullivan, Illinois, at Ace Hardware, Chip’s Marine, or Sullivan 66, formerly Howy’s Lakeside, located five miles south of Sullivan on Highway 32.  Hunters may also pick up roving tree stand permits at the Lake Shelbyville Project Office, Ace Hardware and Craig’s Sporting Goods in Shelbyville.

For more information about the Lake Shelbyville tree stand policy, contact the Environmental Stewardship Department at 217-774-3951, ext. 7049.

title: STATE FAIR RECORD
full_story:
Illinois’ two state fairs drew over 1 million combined visitors for the second year in a row, the governor’s office announced Tuesday.

About 714,000 visitors attended the Springfield fair, while a record 287,000 visited the one in Du Quoin.  Springfield’s attendance was the third highest in its history but set a new single-day attendance record of nearly 104,000 visitors on Friday, August 21st.

The Springfield fair also set a pair of concert attendance records with both Ella Langley and Lainey Wilson drawing 15,533 fans to sold-out shows.

Other featured concerts included The Chicks and Wiz Khalifa.  The Springfield fair sold 72,143 concert tickets, which set a new overall record for grandstand performances.

The fair also featured the traditional 800-pound butter cow sculpture and political events for the state’s primary parties.

While both Democrats and Republicans stressed affordability concerns in party messaging at the fair, Illinois’ fairs were some of the most affordable in the Midwest, according to a comparison conducted by Governor JB Pritzker’s office.

The average cost for a family of four to attend Illinois’ state fairs, including parking, entry tickets, two ride passes and food, was $145, according to the office.

Fair organizers made a concerted effort to make food more affordable.  Promotions offered daily $5 classic fair food options and $3 sample-sized portions at the Village of Cultures, where food from more than 15 nationalities was on display.

Entry to the fair for adults cost $5 and rose to $10 on Fridays and Saturdays.  It cost $3 for seniors and was free for kids up to 12.  A Tuesday “TWOsday” promotion also offered $2 entry for adults and seniors and $2 carnival ride fare.

Dedicated carnival riders could pay $80 for unlimited access to all rides for the full eleven days, or $90 if they wanted to add access to the giant slide, which would otherwise cost $4 per run.

For the first year ever, the Route 66 experience at the fairgrounds also boasted a 25-foot-tall Cozy Dog sculpture, an ode to the Illinois family that first popularized serving corn-battered hot dogs on a stick at the 1946 Illinois State Fair.

The visitors fueled the economy in areas around the fairs, according to IDOA Director Jerry Costello II.

“When more than a million people attend our State Fairs, they’re not just spending money inside the gates,” Costello said in a statement.  “They’re staying in hotels, eating in restaurants, filling their cars with gas, shopping locally and supporting businesses throughout the area.”

Planning for the 2027 state fairs is underway, according to the governor’s office.  The Illinois State Fair in Springfield will run August 12th through 22nd, while the Du Quoin State Fair will run August 27th through September 6th.

title: APPLICATION PERIOD OPENS
full_story:
The Office of the Illinois State Fire Marshal (OSFM) announced the application period is now open for the FY27 Small Equipment Grant Program.  OSFM will award a total of $6 million to eligible fire departments, fire protection districts and not-for-profit ambulance services across Illinois to purchase small firefighting and emergency medical equipment.

For FY27, OSFM has increased the maximum grant award to $50,000, nearly doubling the previous maximum of $26,000.  During the FY26 grant cycle, OSFM awarded nearly $6 million to 264 fire departments, fire protection districts and EMS providers across the state.

Interested departments and ambulance services must submit applications electronically utilizing the application portal that can be found on the agency’s website.

This program is an innovative approach to a problem that has long caused difficulties for the fire departments and not-for-profit ambulance services in Illinois, particularly those that have hardships in generating the necessary revenue for small equipment.  The grants allow eligible applicants the opportunity to purchase small tools and equipment that they may otherwise not be able to purchase.  Most Illinois fire departments, fire protection districts, and township fire departments are eligible to apply.  In addition, stand-alone, not-for-profit ambulance service providers are eligible to apply.

Pre-qualification requirements include Being NFIRS and NERIS compliant for the previous two years, and being pre-qualified with SAM.gov and the State of Illinois Grantee Portal.

Additional information including the application can be found here: https://sfm.illinois.gov/currentfocus/fy-27-small-equipment-grant-.html
